measure: PUBLIC SOURCE REACHABILITY AND PARSEABILITY — a count of sources probed
not_a: an incident count for the world
count_grammar: n counts SOURCES PROBED, the same grammar as effect-binding's 'tool-call servers probed'. It is never pooled with bank-item n and never appears in a mean. REACHABLE means the source answered 200 with a documented shape; UNCHECKABLE means it answered but the body was not the documented shape; UNREACHABLE means it did not answer. These are DIFFERENT facts and are never summed into a single figure that would read like a score.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
sources.note: Known-exploited CVE catalog. Authoritative US list; a CISA KEV entry means exploitation is observed in the wild, not that a product is unsafe in general.

sources.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database CVE API 2.0
sources.note: totalResults is the catalog's own count of CVE records; it is a catalog size, not a measurement of this estate.

sources.name: GitHub Security Advisory Database API
sources.note: GHSA advisories, newest first. Anonymous rate-limited; the count is the page size actually served, not the catalog total.

sources.name: OSV.dev vulnerability query (npm ecosystem)
sources.note: POST query for one named package. A package's advisory count is a fact about that package, not a score for anything.

sources.name: MITRE CVE Services API (single record)
sources.note: Record-level probe: proves the CVE Services API answers a named record. It says nothing about the catalog's completeness.

sources.name: Go vulnerability database index
sources.note: Module index, not advisory records. Counted as a source that answered, not as an advisory count.

unpinned_findings.name: AI Incident Database
unpinned_findings.observed: 404 (the site is a Gatsby SPA; /api/incidents is not an API route)
unpinned_findings.reason: NO PUBLIC MACHINE-READABLE API. The site serves HTML only; the incident corpus lives in the project's private database and is published as a static Excel export, not a queryable feed. There is no URL a daily run can poll that yields incident rows.
unpinned_findings.consequence: AI incident coverage CANNOT be measured continuously from a public endpoint today. It is a real gap, and it is a gap in the SOURCE, not in our reader.
unpinned_findings.next: Ask the AIID maintainers for a public incident JSON/CSV export path, or ingest their published Excel export on a slower cadence. Until then this row stays a published gap.

unpinned_findings.name: NVD CVE 2.0 annual JSON feed
unpinned_findings.observed: 200 but ~42 MB gzipped per year, and the probe timed out mid-transfer
unpinned_findings.reason: ANSWERS, but is too large for a daily poll and too coarse for one (annual file). The API endpoint is pinned instead.
unpinned_findings.consequence: Covered by the nvd-cve-api row. Not a gap; a scale mismatch, resolved by pinning the API.
unpinned_findings.next: None. If a daily n is wanted, use the NVD API with a date window.

unpinned_findings.name: MITRE ATLAS legacy dist/ATLAS.yaml
unpinned_findings.observed: 200 but the file's own first line says it is deprecated and no longer updated
unpinned_findings.reason: Answers, but is a DEPRECATED release. Pinning it would measure a corpus that no longer moves.
unpinned_findings.consequence: Superseded by the atlas-current row, which is resolved from the release manifest.

unpinned_findings.name: npm registry bulk advisories
unpinned_findings.reason: Answers to POST with an advisory list body. Not a GET endpoint.
unpinned_findings.consequence: Not pinned as a GET source. npm advisories are already reachable through the pinned OSV and GHSA rows.
unpinned_findings.next: Add as a POST source only if npm-specific coverage is ever required.

unpinned_findings.name: Sigstore transparency log (api.sigstore.dev)
unpinned_findings.observed: DNS resolution failed on the probing host
unpinned_findings.reason: Host did not resolve from this machine at probe time. The Rekor log IS reachable and is pinned.
unpinned_findings.consequence: One transparency log is covered. The second host was not reachable here, so it is not claimed as covered.
unpinned_findings.next: Re-probe from the scheduled host; a DNS failure at one machine is not proof the source is gone.

unpinned_findings.name: ENISA/CERT-EU security advisories
unpinned_findings.reason: Serves HTML, not a documented machine-readable feed. Counting its HTML byte length as an advisory count would be inventing a number.
unpinned_findings.consequence: NOT covered. A real, named gap in EU-level advisory coverage.
unpinned_findings.next: Look for a documented RSS/JSON feed from CERT-EU; until then, publish the gap.

unpinned_findings.name: Eclipse Foundation security advisories
unpinned_findings.reason: HTML listing page, no documented machine-readable feed at this URL.
unpinned_findings.consequence: NOT covered as a feed. Named gap.
unpinned_findings.next: Check for a JSON/CSV export of the advisory list.

method_note: Every row is derived from the fetched bytes by a fixed rule; body_sha256 lets a later reader recompute the row from the same bytes. No row is scored, weighted or ranked. A source that answers 200 with a shape we cannot read is UNCHECKABLE, never 0 and never 'clean'. unpinned_findings records sources that were probed and did NOT qualify for a pinned URL — the gap stays visible instead of vanishing from the registry.
